habitat: Pairs or small groups on damp ground, near water, in vleis, plantations, agricultural lands, playing fields and suburban gardens. It roosts in tall trees.
summary: A common resident. A heavy brown ibis with a decurved bill and a red culmen, a white cheek stripe and an iridescent pink shoulder. The identification line calls the body greenish-black. The immature is dull and fluffy-headed. The call is a raucous Ha! ha-a-a. The Kemp name Hadedah Ibis and the code RB were left unchanged.

bill.shape: Decurved, fairly short, with a red culmen.

head.pattern: Head and neck dull grey-brown, with a white cheek stripe.

upperparts.pattern: The identification line says the rest is greenish-black with an iridescent shoulder. The description says a heavy brown body and an iridescent pink shoulder.

wings.pattern: Iridescent pink shoulder. Broad wings in flight.

viewNotes.note: Brown body, decurved bill and a white cheek stripe.
White cheek stripe. The culmen is red.
Iridescent pink shoulder. The identification line also says greenish-black.
Broad wings and an iridescent shoulder.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A raucous 'Ha! ha-a-a… ha-ha-a-a…', often from several birds together, when perched or in flight. The grade A flight call is from Kruger, near Skukuza. The filename is XC1146089-20260511_KNP_AKaramitsos_XA60_A025C090_260511NP_SLE_-3dB_HI.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The body is brown in the description and greenish-black on the identification line, so no single body colour is stored. Grey-brown is not a vocabulary colour. The grade A flight call is from Kruger. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login brewmaster is credited. The Kemp name Hadedah Ibis and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.
